questions.title: Which syndrome has 44+XXY chromosomes?
questions.question: Which syndrome has 44+XXY chromosomes?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Down syndrome is trisomy 21, an extra copy of chromosome 21 giving 47 chromosomes overall, and it is unrelated to the sex chromosomes -- it can occur in either a 44+XX (female) or 44+XY (male) background, never written as 44+XXY, so it does not match this genotype.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Turner syndrome is the opposite pattern to the one described: a missing, not an extra, sex chromosome, written 44+XO, giving only 45 chromosomes in total. It affects females with an underdeveloped genital system, so both the count (45, not 47) and the sex-chromosome constitution rule it out here.
explanations.C: Correct. Klinefelter syndrome is a sex-chromosome aneuploidy in males caused by non-disjunction that leaves an extra X chromosome, giving the constitution 44+XXY -- 44 autosomes (22 pairs) plus X, X and Y -- for 47 chromosomes in total, the same notation this question's printed answer key uses. Clinically the extra X causes small, firm testes with reduced fertility, and often gynaecomastia and a taller-than-average build, but the genotype itself, 44+XXY, is what this question is testing directly.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Edward's syndrome is trisomy 18, an extra copy of chromosome 18, again a purely autosomal trisomy independent of the sex chromosomes, so it is never written as 44+XXY.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Cri-du-chat syndrome is a partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5, not a whole extra or missing chromosome, and it has nothing to do with the sex chromosomes, so the 44+XXY genotype does not describe it.

questions.learning_objective: State the chromosomal formula of Klinefelter syndrome and distinguish it from Turner, Down, Edward and cri-du-chat syndromes.

questions.title: Chromosomal formula of a boy with Down's syndrome
questions.question: A boy having Down's syndrome is characterized by a chromosomal formula:

explanations.A: Incorrect. 44+XO is Turner syndrome's formula (45 chromosomes total, one missing sex chromosome), and it describes a female phenotype -- it neither carries a Y chromosome for a boy nor reflects Down syndrome's extra autosome.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 44+XXY is Klinefelter syndrome, an extra sex chromosome (47 total) in a male, not an extra autosome -- Down syndrome's defect is on chromosome 21, not on the sex chromosomes, so this formula does not describe it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 45+XX describes a female (XX) constitution with an extra autosomal pair counted (45, consistent with trisomy) but the wrong sex chromosomes for "a boy" -- the stem specifies a male, which needs XY, not XX.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 43+XY would mean one fewer autosomal pair than normal (a monosomy) together with a normal male XY pair, giving 45 chromosomes overall -- the opposite direction of change from trisomy 21, which adds a chromosome rather than losing one.
explanations.E: Correct. Down syndrome is trisomy 21: one extra copy of chromosome 21 on top of the normal 44 autosomes (22 pairs), most often from meiotic non-disjunction. In this source's own "44+" autosome-pair-count notation, the trisomic pair is written as the extra, giving 45+XY for an affected male (47 chromosomes in total) -- the sex chromosomes are unaffected, so a boy with Down syndrome is still XY, just with the extra chromosome-21 material carried alongside the pair count.

questions.title: Turner's syndrome genotype
questions.question: Turner's syndrome has the following genotype:

explanations.A: Incorrect. 44+XY is the normal male constitution (46 chromosomes total), not an aneuploidy at all, so it cannot be Turner syndrome's genotype.
explanations.B: Correct. Turner syndrome is a sex-chromosome monosomy: one X chromosome is missing entirely, giving the constitution 44+X (45 chromosomes total, sometimes written 44+XO to make the missing chromosome explicit). It affects only females -- there being no Y chromosome to begin with -- and clinically presents with short stature and an underdeveloped (streak) genital system, but the genotype 44+X (45 chromosomes) is this question's own answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 44+XXY is Klinefelter syndrome, an extra X in a male background (47 chromosomes total) -- the opposite kind of change (gain, not loss) from Turner syndrome's monosomy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 44+XXX ("triple X" or "superfemale") is a female with an extra X chromosome (47 chromosomes total), again a gain rather than the loss that defines Turner syndrome.
explanations.E: Incorrect. 44+XYY ("supermale") is a male with an extra Y chromosome (47 chromosomes total), unrelated to Turner syndrome, which has no Y chromosome and one fewer, not one more, sex chromosome.

questions.learning_objective: State the chromosomal formula of Turner syndrome and distinguish a sex-chromosome monosomy from the trisomies it is commonly listed beside.
